summary: ASTRA Mission Trainer is a free, browser-based training platform that helps young people practice astronaut skills through hands-on simulations. Learners command a return mission from lunar orbit and must make fast, safe decisions in randomized emergencies such as fires, power loss, communication blackouts and stuck airlocks, then review an expert debrief and earn a rank. Ten interactive labs teach real space science: building a Moon base, orbital mechanics, gravity on other worlds, life-support planning, re-entry angles, a Mars landing game, exoplanet habitability, asteroid deflection inspired by NASA's DART mission, and Moon phases. The app works in 11 languages so students worldwide can learn in their own language, and badges keep them motivated. Built with Python and Streamlit, ASTRA uses simplified, clearly labeled models and facts from public NASA missions such as Apollo 13 and the ISS. It is an independent educational project, not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
details: ASTRA Mission Trainer is a free web app where young learners train like astronauts. In Mission Control mode they command a return flight from lunar orbit, watch live oxygen, power, fuel and morale meters, and face six randomized emergencies (fire, power loss, communication blackout, stuck airlock, solar storm, docking misalignment). Each choice has consequences, followed by an expert debrief, a rank and a certificate. Nine more labs teach the science: Moon base design, orbital mechanics, weight on other worlds, life-support planning, re-entry angles, a Mars landing game, exoplanet habitability, asteroid deflection inspired by NASA's DART mission, and Moon phases. Benefits: it builds decision-making and science literacy, works on phones, and supports 11 languages so more students can learn in their own language. A high-contrast mode improves readability. Tools: Python, Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, Altair, deep-translator (Google Translate), GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud. Models are simplified and clearly labeled. Facts and values come from public NASA sources. Creativity: it combines game design, simulation and multilingual access, and randomized emergencies make every run different. AI use: the code, emblem and graphics were generated with Claude (Anthropic) under the author's direction, testing and editing. The project uses no NASA logos or mission identifiers and is not affiliated with NASA.
